news.title: Oil Markets Are Betting on a Surplus That Hasn't Arrived Yet
news.summary: Oil prices have traded in a narrow range over the past few sessions as forecasts of a coming surplus collide with continued attacks and stalled diplomacy in the Middle East. A run of agency reports this month has pushed expectations toward oversupply and weighed on crude. Brent crude was up 1.1% at $92.88 per barrel at 11:50 a.m. ET on Thursday, well below its October levels above 110 dollars but little changed from the start of the week, while WTI crude gained 1.7% to 84.69 dollars per barrel. analysis.summary: Crude oil is range-bound as agency surplus forecasts weigh against Middle East attacks and stalled diplomacy.
analysis.rationale: The text explicitly contrasts downward pressure from agency oversupply forecasts with upward geopolitical risk from Middle East attacks and stalled diplomacy.

news.title: Thanksgiving Gas Prices Could Break a Record Despite Recent Plunge
news.summary: Gasoline prices have fallen nearly 60 cents in a month, but Americans heading out for Thanksgiving could still pay more at the pump than during any previous Thanksgiving. The national average fell to $3.69 per gallon on Friday, according to AAA, down from approximately $4.30 a month ago. GasBuddy expects prices to average $3.62 on Thanksgiving Day, which would surpass the previous holiday record of $3.56 set in 2022. The declines are substantial. analysis.summary: US retail gasoline prices fell sharply over the past month alongside retreating crude and recovering supplies, though Thanksgiving averages may still hit a holiday record.
analysis.rationale: The item focuses on lagging US retail pump prices and references past crude retreats and recovering supplies rather than presenting a clear forward-looking crude catalyst.
